title: Reliable shipment requests

baseline.label: Fictional example, not a repository audit

summary: A customer can request a shipment even when the parcel provider is slow. We record the order and dispatch intent together, then a dispatcher creates or reconciles the shipment. A timeout leaves the outcome unknown until it is confirmed. This example illustrates the report format; no implementation or acceptance test is claimed.
problem: Today the fictional API calls the provider before saving the shipment reference. A provider success followed by a connection loss can leave the customer unsure whether retrying will create another shipment.
goals: One acknowledged request remains visible through restart and provider timeout.
The customer sees Processing until a provider shipment is confirmed.
A repeated request for the same order reuses the same dispatch identity.
non_goals: Change parcel pricing or select another provider.
Claim universal or end-to-end exactly-once delivery.

evidence.source: Fictional baseline defined in this example
evidence.claim: The API currently calls the provider synchronously and then stores provider_ref on Order.

evidence.source: Fictional Parcel Provider contract; verify real provider documentation before implementation
evidence.claim: For illustration only: create is idempotent for the same key and payload for 72 hours; changed payload is rejected; query-by-key can confirm a shipment. This is not a verified provider guarantee.
A local transaction can atomically store business state and durable intent; downstream delivery may repeat.
A timeout does not establish that a remote side effect failed.

evidence.source: Illustrative policy values, pending owner approval and measurement
evidence.claim: At most three reserved create attempts and six reconciliation queries per command. Attempt eligibility closes at 48 hours; an already-authorized call may settle later. Original key retained for all attempts. Numeric values are illustrative, not operational recommendations.

invariants.text: An acknowledged shipment request has durable intent and a visible order status.
A command keeps one key and one payload; repeated execution never chooses a fresh identity.
Only a confirmed provider shipment makes an order Shipped; timeout means Unknown.
Create attempts stop at the configured count or time bound, including after worker restart.

decisions.title: Separate shipment acceptance from provider delivery
decisions.context: The provider creates the external effect, while our system owns the order and dispatch intent. A lost response cannot be repaired safely by blindly starting another request.

options.name: Keep synchronous provider calls
tradeoffs: Customer request depends on provider availability; a lost response leaves no durable recovery instruction.

options.name: Durable command with a dispatcher
tradeoffs: Local acceptance survives provider latency and worker restarts.
Adds processing states, dispatch ownership, and reconciliation work.

options.name: Publish directly to a broker after saving
tradeoffs: Introduces a dual-write gap unless publication is coupled to the local commit.

consequences: Order and ShippingCommand are written in one local transaction.
Provider delivery happens outside that transaction and may repeat with the same identity.
The UI must distinguish Processing, Shipped, and Needs review.
The provider assumption E2 is decision-critical and must be verified before accepting this ADR.

views.title: Big picture · ownership stays clear
views.note: System context. The external provider remains authoritative for shipment creation; our system adds durable dispatch intent and reconciliation to its ownership of order state. The same actors remain landmarks.

fields.responsibility: owns order and durable dispatch intent

edges.label: Create / query shipment; provider owns effect

views.title: Entity changes · retain the old model
views.note: Logical entities, not a complete physical schema. Explicit counts describe relationships. Order keeps its identity; provider_ref moves into ShippingCommand. A Needs review command still blocks creation of another identity for that order.

views.title: Service structure · the external call moves
views.note: Runtime responsibilities. Database arrows describe reads/writes, not remote transaction membership. The removed API → provider call remains visible in Changes; its replacement goes through the dispatcher.

flows.title: Service interaction · accept a durable request
flows.contract: An authorization check precedes a local transaction. Order and intent commit before a success response is acknowledged. Repeated requests reuse the existing command, including Unknown and Needs review; they never choose a fresh key. The dispatcher never participates in the customer transaction.

steps.label: Request shipment for order O1
steps.detail: The API checks that the customer can dispatch this order.

steps.label: Commit order + dispatch intent
steps.detail: One local transaction stores Processing, command C1, key K1, and the immutable shipment payload. A unique order_id constraint resolves concurrent requests and keeps Needs review identity-blocking.

steps.label: Commit acknowledged
steps.detail: The intent and order are durable before the API acknowledges the request.

steps.label: Return Processing and tracking link
steps.detail: The customer can observe Processing without waiting for the provider.

steps.label: Claim pending command C1
steps.detail: A short lease and version token fence local updates. A persisted attempt reservation happens before each external create call.

flows.title: Third-party flow · confirmed, unknown, repeated
flows.contract: Illustrative provider contract E2 must be verified. The dispatcher sends shipment address and order reference over authenticated HTTPS using scoped provider credentials. Create uses immutable key K1 and payload; query-by-key reconciles uncertain outcomes. Only the dispatcher owns retries: at most three reserved creates and six reserved queries; eligibility closes at 48 hours (illustrative E5). Already-authorized calls may settle later. Backoff uses jitter; retries never choose a fresh key. Needs review stops further automatic attempts but preserves the identity. Provider effects cannot be rolled back by a database transaction. No webhook is assumed.

participants.name: Order database
participants.role: order + command state; no remote atomicity

steps.label: Create shipment with key K1
steps.detail: The dispatcher uses the stored immutable payload and key after reserving an attempt in a local transaction.

steps.label: Return confirmed shipment P1
steps.detail: The provider is authoritative for P1. The reply must match the command identity.

steps.label: Confirm C1 and mark O1 Shipped
steps.detail: One local transaction stores P1 and Shipped using the lease version. A stale worker cannot overwrite newer confirmation.

scenarios.title: Response is lost after possible creation

steps.label: Create shipment with key K1
steps.detail: P1 may be created even if the response is lost.

steps.label: Timeout: outcome remains unknown
steps.detail: Timeout is not a provider refusal and does not authorize a new key.

steps.label: Persist Unknown; order stays Processing
steps.detail: The customer is not told Shipped or Failed. The persisted attempt count survives restart.

steps.label: Query existing shipment by key K1
steps.detail: Reconciliation confirms the previous effect before any further create attempt. Query unavailability leaves the command Unknown.

steps.label: Confirm prior shipment P1
steps.detail: This scenario assumes the provider can return the record under E2.

steps.label: Confirm P1; mark order Shipped
steps.detail: One fenced local transaction stores the confirmed reference and customer-visible Shipped state.

scenarios.title: A stale worker repeats the external call

steps.label: Repeat create with the same key K1
steps.detail: Worker interruption may repeat a call. Same identity and payload are necessary even with a local lease.

steps.label: Return the same shipment P1
steps.detail: Under E2, the provider associates the replay with P1 rather than creating P2. This claim depends on the unverified provider contract.

steps.label: Confirm only if lease version is current
steps.detail: A stale local update is discarded. Existing confirmation is monotonic and remains visible.

steps.label: Eligibility closes; outcome unresolved
steps.detail: The time window closes, or create/query budgets are exhausted and all already-authorized attempts have settled or timed out. No new attempt is authorized.

steps.label: Mark command and order Needs review
steps.detail: One local transaction updates both records with the current lease version. The original key and payload are retained.

steps.label: Stop automatic attempts; preserve K1
steps.detail: A repeated customer request returns the existing Needs review identity. Operators can investigate K1 without authorizing another shipment. A verified late confirmation may still resolve the original effect.

pseudocode.title: Accept locally; deliver and reconcile separately
pseudocode.code:
accept_shipment(customer, order_id):
  authorize(customer, order_id)
  LOCAL TRANSACTION:
    lock order
    if order is shipped: return existing shipment status
    if command exists (including unknown or needs_review):
      return its existing status and tracking identity
    insert command(key = stable_random_id(), immutable_payload, attempts = 0)
    set order.status = processing
  COMMIT
  return Processing                         // INV1, AC1

dispatch(command_id):
  LOCAL TRANSACTION:
    claim eligible command with lease_version
    if confirmed or needs_review: return
    if elapsed >= 48 hours or attempts >= 3:
      command = needs_review; order = needs_review
      COMMIT; return                         // illustrative bounds; INV4
    reserve attempt; increment attempts
  COMMIT                                     // no provider I/O in transaction
  call provider.create(stored_key, immutable_payload)  // INV2, AC4
  // Already-authorized call may settle after eligibility closes.
  on confirmed response:
    LOCAL TRANSACTION:
      if lease_version is current:
        store provider_ref; command = confirmed; order = shipped
    COMMIT                                   // INV3, AC2
  on timeout or ambiguous response:
    persist unknown only if lease_version is current
    schedule reconciliation with bounded backoff + jitter  // AC3
  on verified permanent refusal:
    mark_review_with_fencing(command, order, lease_version)

reconcile_unknown(command):
  LOCAL TRANSACTION:
    claim current lease_version
    if confirmed or needs_review: return
    if elapsed >= 48 hours or queries >= 6:
      command = needs_review; order = needs_review
      COMMIT; return
    reserve query; increment queries
  COMMIT
  query provider by stored_key                // never a new identity
  if confirmed: confirm with current lease_version
  else if provider explicitly confirms no effect and budget remains:
    schedule dispatch with SAME key and payload
  else if budget expired:
    mark_review_with_fencing(command, order, lease_version) // INV4, AC5
  else:
    keep unknown; schedule bounded reconciliation

mark_review_with_fencing(command, order, lease_version):
  LOCAL TRANSACTION:
    if lease_version is current and command is not confirmed:
      command = needs_review; order = needs_review
      preserve key, payload, and tracking identity
  COMMIT

acceptance.title: Request survives a dispatcher restart
acceptance.given: an authorized customer has an order ready to ship
acceptance.when: the shipment request is acknowledged and the dispatcher restarts before contacting the provider
then: The customer still sees Processing and can use the same tracking link.
Delivery work resumes for the acknowledged request after restart.

acceptance.title: Confirmed shipment becomes visible
then: The customer sees Shipped with the tracking reference for P1.
Refreshing the order preserves the confirmed status.

acceptance.title: Lost response does not report failure
acceptance.given: the provider may have created a shipment but its response was lost
acceptance.when: the request times out and reconciliation later confirms P1
then: The customer sees Processing while the outcome is unresolved.
The customer then sees Shipped with P1 rather than being asked to start a new shipment.

acceptance.title: Repeated requests retain one identity
acceptance.given: the same order already has a Processing request and the illustrative provider contract E2 holds
acceptance.when: the customer repeats the request and two worker executions overlap
then: The customer receives the same processing/tracking identity.
The external provider receives the same key and payload for any repeated create call.
The provider exposes the same shipment P1 for the repeated calls under E2.

acceptance.title: Unresolved delivery stops at its budget
acceptance.given: a request remains unresolved under the illustrative policy E5
acceptance.when: attempt eligibility closes, or create/query budgets are exhausted after already-authorized attempts settle or time out
then: The customer sees Needs review instead of a false Shipped status.
No further automatic attempt is authorized for the command; any previously authorized call may settle later.
The provider receives at most three create attempts and six queries for the original identity.
Repeating the customer request returns the same Needs review tracking identity.
An operator can investigate the original identity without starting another shipment request.

acceptance.title: Existing shipped orders remain readable
acceptance.given: an order was shipped before this change
acceptance.when: a customer opens it after the compatibility migration
then: The original shipment reference and Shipped status remain visible.
Opening the order triggers no new shipment create call.

rollout.entry: Verify provider contract E2; approve policy values E5.
rollout.change: Add command storage and new read states; keep legacy provider_ref readable.
rollout.exit: Old and new readers render existing shipped orders (AC6).
rollout.recovery: Disable new writer; old records are still readable.

rollout.change: Backfill confirmed legacy references into completed commands without making provider calls.
rollout.exit: Reference parity is checked; unconfirmed legacy orders are reconciled or quarantined.
rollout.recovery: Keep legacy references; repair/re-run backfill with stable command IDs.

rollout.entry: No legacy writer can bypass the active-command constraint.
rollout.change: Enable durable acceptance and dispatcher for eligible orders.
rollout.exit: AC1–AC5 pass; pending age and Needs review volume meet owner-approved bounds.
rollout.recovery: Stop new dispatches; retain Processing intents. Reconcile in-flight provider effects; do not re-enable blind legacy retries.

rollout.entry: Observation window approved; parity holds; no old reader remains.
rollout.change: Retire direct provider calls and legacy provider_ref only after explicit approval.
rollout.exit: Legacy access is absent and completed commands serve all shipment references.
rollout.recovery: After field removal, use forward repair or restore from preserved migration data; binary rollback alone cannot recreate lost data.

risks.risk: Provider idempotency/query semantics differ from E2.
risks.mitigation: Verify the real API/version before accepting D1; choose another reconciliation strategy if necessary.

risks.risk: Migration activates both old and new create paths.
risks.mitigation: Gate activation on legacy writer retirement and quarantine unresolved legacy orders.

risks.risk: Backlog exceeds the illustrative retry window.
risks.mitigation: Observe pending age; stop at the configured bound and expose Needs review. Agree staffing and alert threshold before activation.

questions.question: Does the actual provider support key-bound payloads, retention, and query-by-key?
questions.affects: D1 and AC3/AC4; E2 is a blocking assumption for implementation.

questions.question: What retry budget and pending-age alert fit measured latency and operations capacity?
questions.affects: E5, INV4, AC5, and rollout activation.

questions.question: Who owns Needs review and what response time is required?
questions.affects: Operational acceptance and readiness for stage 3.
